newsitem.title: THAILAND: FORECAST - Two-tier baht system seen staying 4-8 weeks.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Two-tier baht system seen staying 4-8 weeks.

text.p: Economic consultancy IDEA said on Thursday it expected the Bank of Thailand to maintain its two-tier baht exchange rate system for at least another four to eight weeks.

The research agency said in a statement that offshore currency markets expected the Thai central bank to keep the three-week-old measure to curb market attacks on the baht until domestic economic indicators showed more positive signs.

It said some foreign fund managers and currency players with long baht positions started making profits on steady gains of the offshore baht by squaring off their maturing contracts in the spot market rather than rolling them over forward.

"With the BoT likely to keep the current two-tier market intact, at least for another four-eight weeks till domestic economic figures show more positive signs, the strategy will be to sell USD/THB on upticks, and collect USD back towards sub-24.00...," it said.
The baht rallied to its 13-year high of 23.800/23.900 to the dollar in offshore markets late on Thursday morning from 24.570/24.600 at the opening.
In the domestic market, the baht hovered at a relatively steady 25.831/25.838.

The research house quoted market talk as saying that more than $1 billion of long dollar/baht positions were still held by foreign players, including long-term U.S. fund managers, despite Thailand's policy since mid-May to block short-term funds used by speculators to attack the baht.
It said with the two-tier system expected to remain for a while, some of the long baht positions held offshore may be traded by their holders to take advantage of the strong offshore baht.

"Criticially, the strategy here seems like buying USD/THB to sell. And hopefully in the process more USD-sales can be executed without depressing USD/THB tremendously in the extremely thin market," IDEA said.
